headline: Cyera acquires Oasis Security for $1B to safeguard proliferating AI agents
summary: Data security firm Cyera, valued at $12 billion, is set to acquire Oasis Security for approximately $1 billion, mostly in cash. Oasis specializes in securing non-human identities, particularly AI agents.
details: Data security company Cyera, recently valued at $12 billion, has signed a letter of intent to acquire Oasis Security for approximately $1 billion. The deal is expected to be paid mostly in cash, with the remainder in Cyera shares.

Oasis Security focuses on protecting non-human identities, primarily AI agents. As AI agents proliferate, companies require cybersecurity software to monitor their behavior and manage their access permissions to other systems.

Founded in 2022, Oasis has raised about $195 million from investors including Accel, Craft Ventures, and Cyberstarts. This acquisition underscores a rapidly expanding market for cybersecurity solutions against AI-weaponized threats.

Cyera, which shares investors Accel and Cyberstarts with Oasis, has been actively expanding through acquisitions. It recently purchased Index Ventures-backed Ryft and the less-than-one-year-old Genie Security.
Post-acquisition, Cyera plans to integrate Oasis’s advanced technology into its unified identity and data security platform. This aims to create a comprehensive solution for enterprise protection.
Despite surpassing $150 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR), the five-year-old Cyera is not yet profitable. The company has raised a total of about $2.3 billion in funding to date.

headline: Andrew Ng's LearnVector gets $100M from Coursera for AI-powered 1-to-1 learning
summary: Andrew Ng's new AI company, LearnVector, secured a $100M investment from Coursera. It aims to transform education from one-to-many classrooms to personalized one-to-one learning experiences, adapting to each student's needs and pace.
details: AI pioneer Andrew Ng has launched LearnVector, a new company backed by a $100M investment from Coursera. LearnVector aims to revolutionize education by creating personalized one-to-one learning experiences, moving beyond traditional one-to-many models.

Ng highlights that while online courses expanded access, the core 'how' of learning remains largely unchanged. Current AI chatbots, without proper guardrails, can harm learning by promoting cognitive offloading and lacking trustworthiness, failing to provide a true education.

LearnVector's approach involves building a custom learning guide for each person. It will plan a path, adapt to individual learning styles, and patiently stay with the learner until new skills are mastered, ensuring accurate and relevant content.

The company plans to collaborate closely with Coursera and Udemy, leveraging Coursera's trusted library of materials from authoritative sources. This partnership aims to bring high-quality, trustworthy learning to a wider audience.

LearnVector is currently heads-down building its products, with a target launch by early 2027. The Mountain View-based team is actively hiring for roles in agentic systems, product pedagogy, AI teaching innovation, and full-stack software development.
